========================================================================
COMPREHENSIVE PHONETIC DICTIONARY OF ENGLISH WORDS ENDING IN A SCHWA
========================================================================

This file lists every word in the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary whose final syllable
has a vowel sound of a schwa. In General American English and the CMU Pronouncing
Dictionary, the schwa sound has two primary representations:

1. PURE SCHWA (ARPAbet: 'AH0' -> IPA: '/ə/'):
   This is the standard, unstressed mid-central vowel. Examples include the final
   syllables of words like 'sofa' (/ˈsoʊfə/), 'diet' (/dˈaɪət/), 'finest' (/fˈaɪnəst/),
   'pencil' (/pˈɛnsəl/), and 'about' (/əbˈaʊt/).

2. R-COLORED SCHWA (ARPAbet: 'ER0' -> IPA: '/ər/' or '[ɚ]'):
   This is the r-colored or rhoticized central vowel (sometimes referred to as a 'schwer').
   Examples include the final syllables of words like 'butter' (/bˈʌtər/), 'actor' (/ˈæktər/),
   'teacher' (/tˈiʧər/), and 'doctor' (/dˈɑktər/).

Below, words are listed alphabetically under their respective phonetic categories.
For each word, we display its matching pronunciation(s) in IPA format (inside slashes)
and its corresponding raw CMU (ARPAbet) phonemes.
